events.description: Nice founded by Phocaean Greek colonists and named Nikaia in honour of a victory over the Ligurians.
Saracens pillaged and burned Nice in 859 and again in 880.
Nice attacked by combined Franco-Ottoman forces of Francis I and Barbarossa; city surrendered and was pillaged, with 2,500 captives taken.
Nice captured by Nicolas Catinat; restored to Savoy in 1696.
Nice conquered by the armies of the French First Republic.
Nice annexed to France following a plebiscite on 15–16 April 1860; Italian was immediately replaced by French as official language.
American paratroopers entered Nice on 30 August 1944, liberating it from German occupation.
On 14 July 2016, a truck was deliberately driven into a crowd on the Promenade des Anglais; 87 people killed, 434 injured.
